text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users communicate with LLMs through prompts, and prompt engineering means writing clear instructions to get better results. These models are good at tasks like writing, summarising and translating. However, they also have limits. They can make mistakes, give outdated information, or produce false facts. For this reason, it is always wise to check important answers yourself.
